Coventry's population increased by around 28,400 between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021). This semi-automated article highlights some of the most notable changes among the local population.

The population reached nearly 350,000

Between the last two censuses (held in 2011 and 2021), the population of Coventry increased by 8.9%, from just under 317,000 in 2011 to around 345,300 in 2021.

The population here increased by a greater percentage than the overall population of the West Midlands (6.2%), and by a greater percentage than the overall population of England (up 6.6% since the 2011 Census).

In 2021, Coventry was home to around 25.0 people per football pitch-sized piece of land, compared with 22.9 in 2011. This area was among the top 20% most densely populated English local authority areas at the last census.

This article generally uses percentages to enable comparisons over time and between areas. The percentage point change is also used to show the difference between the 2011 and 2021 percentages.

Population growth was higher in Coventry than across the West Midlands

Median age in Coventry

Between the last two censuses, the average (median) age of Coventry increased by one year, from 34 to 35 years of age.

This area had the second-lowest average (median) age in the West Midlands (behind Birmingham) and a lower average (median) age than England (40 years).

The median age is the age of the person in the middle of the group, meaning that one half of the group is younger than that person and the other half is older.

The number of people aged 50 to 64 years rose by around 8,800 (an increase of 18.2%), while the number of residents aged 4 years and under fell by just over 2,000 (9.0% decrease).

The share of residents aged between 50 and 64 years increased by 1.3 percentage points between 2011 and 2021

Family in Coventry

The percentage of households including a couple with dependent children increased in Coventry, but fell across the West Midlands.

In Coventry, the percentage of households including a couple with dependent children rose from 18.2% in 2011 to 19.3% in 2021. During the same period, the regional percentage fell from 19.7% to 19.0%.

The percentage of households including a couple without children in Coventry fell from 13.7% to 13.3%, while the percentage of households including a couple with only non-dependent children increased from 6.1% to 6.4%.

The percentage of households including a couple with dependent children in Coventry increased by 1.2 percentage points

Coventry residents' country of birth

In the latest census, around 242,100 Coventry residents said they were born in England. This represented 70.1% of the local population. The figure has risen from around 240,100 in 2011, which at the time represented 75.8% of Coventry's population.

India was the next most represented, with just over 15,600 Coventry residents reporting this country of birth (4.5%). This figure was up from just over 13,400 in 2011, which at the time represented 4.2% of the population of Coventry.

The number of Coventry residents born in Poland rose from just over 6,400 in 2011 (2.0% of the local population) to just under 8,900 in 2021 (2.6%).

In 2021, 70.1% of Coventry residents reported their country of birth as England

Ethnic groups in Coventry

In 2021, 8.9% of Coventry residents identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category, up from 5.6% in 2011. The 3.3 percentage-point change was the largest increase among high-level ethnic groups in this area.

Across the West Midlands, the percentage of people from the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" ethnic group increased from 3.3% to 4.5%, while across England the percentage increased from 3.5% to 4.2%.

In 2021, 65.5% of people in Coventry identified their ethnic group within the "White" category (compared with 73.8% in 2011), while 18.5% identified their ethnic group within the "Asian, Asian British or Asian Welsh" category (compared with 16.3% the previous decade).

The percentage of people who identified their ethnic group within the "Other" category ("Arab" or "Any other ethnic group") increased from 1.7% in 2011 to 3.7% in 2021.

There are many factors that may be contributing to the changing ethnic composition of England and Wales, such as differing patterns of ageing, fertility, mortality, and migration. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses.

Read the bulletin Ethnic group, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 8.9% of usual residents in Coventry identified their ethnic group within the "Black, Black British, Black Welsh, Caribbean or African" category

Religion in Coventry

In 2021, 29.6% of Coventry residents reported having "No religion", up from 23.0% in 2011. The rise of 6.6 percentage points was the largest increase of all broad religious groups in Coventry. Because the census question about religious affiliation is voluntary and has varying response rates, caution is needed when comparing figures between different areas or between censuses.

Across the West Midlands, the percentage of residents who described themselves as having "No religion" increased from 22.0% to 32.9%, while across England the percentage increased from 24.8% to 36.7%.

In 2021, 43.9% of people in Coventry described themselves as Christian (down from 53.7%), while 10.4% described themselves as Muslim (up from 7.5% the decade before).

There are many factors that can cause changes to the religious profile of an area, such as a changing age structure or residents relocating for work or education. Changes may also be caused by differences in the way individuals chose to self-identify between censuses. Religious affiliation is the religion with which someone connects or identifies, rather than their beliefs or religious practice.

Read the bulletin Religion, England and Wales: Census 2021.

In 2021, 29.6% of usual residents in Coventry reported having "No religion"

Health in Coventry

In 2021, 44.5% of Coventry residents described their health as "very good", increasing from 41.3% in 2011. Those describing their health as "good" fell from 35.7% to 34.9%. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The proportion of Coventry residents describing their health as "very bad" was 1.5% (similar to 2011), while those describing their health as "bad" fell from 5.6% to 4.8%.

These data reflect people’s own opinions in describing their overall health on a five point scale, from very good to very bad.

Census 2021 was conducted during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and rated their health, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

The percentage of people in very good health in Coventry increased by 3.2 percentage points

National identity in Coventry

Coventry saw the West Midlands' joint third-largest percentage-point rise (alongside Rugby) in the proportion of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK (from 14.1% in 2011 to 18.2% in 2021).

Across the region, only Wolverhampton (from 8.9% to 14.0%) and Sandwell (from 8.8% to 13.8%) saw a greater increase in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK.

Every local authority area across the West Midlands saw a rise in the percentage of people who did not identify with any national identity associated with the UK, as the regional percentage grew from 6.2% to 8.7%.

In Census 2021, “British” was moved to the top response option and this may have influenced how people described their national identity. For further information, please see our quality report.

The percentage of people who did not identify with at least one UK national identity in Coventry increased by 4.1 percentage points

Unpaid care in Coventry

In 2021, 4.3% of Coventry residents (aged five years and over) reported providing up to 19 hours of unpaid care each week. This figure decreased from 7.2% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

The decrease in the proportion of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Coventry (2.9 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the West Midlands (2.9 percentage points, from 7.4% to 4.5%). Across England, the proportion fell by 2.8 percentage points, from 7.2% to 4.4%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived and managed their provision of unpaid care, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people (aged five years and over) providing up to 19 hours of weekly unpaid care in Coventry decreased by 2.9 percentage points

Rise in private renting

The increase in the percentage of privately-rented homes was greater in Coventry (4.1 percentage points) than in nearby Warwick (1.1 percentage points).

In Coventry, the percentage of private renting increased from 20.6% in 2011 to 24.7% in 2021. During the same period, the percentage in nearby Warwick increased from 17.9% to 19.0%.

The rate of social renting in Coventry remained at 17.0%, while the rate of home ownership decreased from 60.6% to 57.4%.

Private renting in Coventry increased by 4.1 percentage points

Changing relationships in Coventry

In 2021, 8.1% of Coventry residents (aged 16 years and over) said they had got divorced or dissolved a civil partnership. This figure decreased from 8.5% in 2011.

In 2021, just over 4 in 10 people (40.2%) said they were married or in a registered civil partnership, compared with 41.9% in 2011. The percentage of adults who were never married or in a civil partnership in Coventry increased from 40.1% to 44.0%.

Coventry saw the West Midlands' largest fall in the percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership. This area had the region’s joint third lowest percentage of people aged 16 years and over who had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership (alongside Solihull).

These figures include same-sex marriages and opposite-sex civil partnerships in 2021, neither of which were legally recognised in England and Wales in 2011. Same-sex marriages have been legally recognised in England and Wales since 2014 and opposite-sex civil partnerships have been recognised since 2019.

The percentage of adults who had divorced or dissolved a civil partnership in Coventry decreased by 0.4 percentage points

Employment in Coventry

Of Coventry residents aged 16 years and over, 51.0% said they were employed (excluding full-time students) in 2021, a similar percentage as in 2011 (50.9%).

In 2021, just over 1 in 30 people (3.4%) said they were unemployed, compared with 4.9% in 2011. The percentage of retired Coventry residents decreased from 19.1% to 17.3%.

This area had the region’s second lowest percentage of people aged 16 years and over (excluding full-time students) who were employed. Across the region, only Birmingham, with 47.4%, had a lower percentage.

Census 2021 took place during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic, a period of rapid and unparalleled change; the national lockdown, associated guidance and furlough measures will have affected the labour market and our ability to measure it.

The percentage of people aged 16 years and over who were employed (excluding full-time students) in Coventry increased by 0.1 percentage points

Change in work hours

In 2021, 9.6% of Coventry residents aged 16 years and over and in employment said they worked 15 hours or less per week. This figure decreased from 9.9% in 2011.

While the percentage of people aged 16 years and over and in employment who said they usually worked 15 hours or less per week fell here, across the West Midlands the percentage increased from 9.6% in 2011 to 9.9% in 2021. Across England, the percentage increased from 9.7% to 10.3%.

Working hours may have been affected by the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic.

The percentage of adults who worked 15 hours or less in Coventry decreased by 0.3 percentage points

Disability in Coventry

In 2021, 8.4% of Coventry residents were identified as being disabled and limited a lot. This figure decreased from 10.5% in 2011. These are age-standardised proportions.

Age-standardised proportions are used throughout this section. They enable comparisons between populations over time and across geographies, as they account for differences in the population size and age structure.

In 2021, around 1 in 10 people (10.0%) were identified as being disabled and limited a little, compared with 10.7% in 2011. The proportion of Coventry residents who were not disabled increased from 78.8% to 81.6%.

The decrease in the proportion of residents who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Coventry (2.1 percentage points) was similar to the decrease across the West Midlands (1.9 percentage points, from 9.9% to 8.0%). Across England, the proportion fell by 1.6 percentage points, from 9.1% to 7.5%.

Census 2021 was undertaken during the coronavirus (COVID-19) pandemic. This may have influenced how people perceived their health status and activity limitations, and therefore may have affected how people chose to respond.

Caution should be taken when making comparisons between 2011 and 2021 because of changes in question wording and response options.

The percentage of people who were identified as being disabled and limited a lot in Coventry decreased by 2.1 percentage points
